findings.evidence: template/scripts/candidate_lifecycle.py (diff lines 336-337) sets state = "contribution-integration-pending" for any contribution validated-push receipt. The live path in integration_contour.advance_after_repair decides between pending and review using main_only_reason/equivalent_proofs. The recovery path has no such check, so gates bound to the old identity no longer match. merge_reviewed_contribution would then refuse with "contribution lacks current review" instead of returning the candidate to review. This contradicts publication-queue spec 'Writer resolved a conflict in task content'. The only added test covers the clean recovery case.
findings.summary: Recovery of an interrupted contribution integration repair goes straight to contribution-integration-pending without checking whether the writer changed task content. The spec says changed content must return to review on the new base.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/post_review_finalization.py require_base_in_target (diff lines 613-619) runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor base target_head` only. The head-containment check is left to the select_checks --contribution-base gate, and none of the new code or tests shows finalization failing closed on it. Spec: 'scoped to that base, which the head and the target SHALL contain. An unproven contribution base SHALL be refused.'
findings.summary: The platform-lifecycle spec says the contribution base must be contained in both the head and the target. The new finalize guard checks only the target.
